description: Risk-controlled, qrel-free stopping rule for the regularized partial-information rank aggregator (regularized_aggregation_pilot_v1). Reuses the same frozen SciDocs q50/k15 exhaustive gpt-4o-mini pairwise oracle, the same 15/35 dev/test split, and the same frozen linear_decay regularization schedule. No live provider calls, no new judgments, no qrel leakage into the stopping decision itself.
max_simulated_budget_rationale: Matches the task's own stop/go criterion ('needs more than 60% of comparisons -> insufficiently useful'); capping the expensive per-step simulation horizon here is a computational-cost decision, not a scientific one -- any (tau, m) setting that fails to trigger patience within this cap is recorded as 'capped, not stopped' and evaluated at the cap budget, which already disqualifies it from being a practically useful setting under the task's own bar.
threshold_selection_rationale: Selected on the 15-query dev split (random order only), before any test-set metric was computed. tau in {0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30} x patience in {2, 3, 5} were tried (15 combinations; recorded in REPORT.md Phase 4/9). tau<=0.15 essentially never triggers within the 60%-budget cap (9-15 of 15 dev queries capped), failing the H1 practical-savings target outright. tau>=0.30 triggers very early (median ~11-17% budget) but with mean nDCG 0.07-0.14 below exhaustive-BM25 gap recovery well under 50%. tau=0.20 was the smallest threshold that reliably triggers well inside the 60% cap for a majority of dev queries (13-15/15 not capped, depending on patience) while keeping severe-harm at 0/15 across every (tau, patience) combination tried. Patience m=3 was fixed (not swept per-tau) as a reasonable middle value between m=2 (marginally noisier, more capped-avoidance) and m=5 (materially higher median budget, e.g. 43.8% vs 32.4% at tau=0.20, crossing the H1 40% target). The two sensitivity settings vary only tau (0.15 more conservative, 0.25 more aggressive) at the same fixed patience, isolating the threshold's effect.
premature_stop_qrel_label_definition: the stopped top-k differs from the exhaustive top-k AND (exhaustive nDCG@10 - stopped nDCG@10) >= 0.02 -- a qrel-bearing EVALUATION label only, computed after the stopping decision, never fed back into it.
premature_instability_qrelfree_definitio: the stopped top-k set differs from the exhaustive top-k set (no qrels; a purely structural instability signal, reported separately from the qrel-bearing label above).
correction: Holm, family = the 5 pre-registered primary comparisons above, evaluated only on the 35-query held-out test split, random acquisition order
leakage_controls: stopping.py's public functions take only (candidates, revealed-so-far outcomes, qrels-free BM25 prior, frozen schedule, current qrels-free utilities) -- no qrels, no oracle object, no unrevealed pair's actual cached outcome (only its own simulated hypothetical outcomes), no exhaustive ranking

the counterfactual worst-case statistic is computed purely from currently-revealed evidence plus self-generated hypothetical outcomes for still-unrevealed pairs -- it never reads the oracle's cached answer for those pairs

the premature-stop qrel label and severe-harm rate are evaluation-only, computed strictly after the stopping decision, in a separate code path (run_stopping_rule_pilot.py's analyze stage) that stopping.py itself has no access to
